svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "Forelimbs of four mammals: human, cat, whale and bat."], [1, "Each has one upper bone: the humerus."], [3, "Two forearm bones: radius and ulna."], [5, "Wrist bones: carpals."], [7, "Palm bones: metacarpals."], [9, "Digit bones: phalanges, up to five digits (pentadactyl)."], [11.5, "Same bones, different functions: evidence of common ancestry."]]
svg.title: Homologous structures: the pentadactyl limb
svg.desc: The forelimb skeletons of a human, a cat, a whale and a bat with humerus, radius and ulna, carpals, metacarpals and phalanges colour-coded to show the shared pattern.
svg.text: Same colour = same bone. Not to scale: each limb drawn to a similar height.

g.data-info: One bone in the upper arm (or upper part of the limb).
Grasping, walking, swimming and flying limbs share one plan: the pentadactyl limb. This suggests a common ancestor: homologous structures, adapted by divergent evolution.
